sections.description:
Short title extent and commencement

PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT, 1972
PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT,
1972
1. Short title, extent and commencement.‑‑(1) This Act
may be called the Peoples' Finance Corporation Act, 1972.
(2) It extends to the whole of
Pakistan,
(3) it shall come into force at
once

Definitions

PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT, 1972
PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT,
1972
2. Definitions.‑In this Act, unless there is anything
repugnant in the: subject or context,‑---
(a) "Board" means the
Board of Directors of the Corporation';
(b) "Chairman" means the Chairman of the Board;
(c) "Corporation" means the Peoples' Finance Corporation
established under section 3 ; .
(d) "debtor" Includes
a guarantor ;
(e) "Director" means a director of the Corporation ;
(f) "firm" means a
firm registered under the. Partnership Act, 1932 (IX of 1932) ;
(g) "loan" Includes
guarantee or indemnity which the Corporation may give on behalf of a borrower ;
(h) "Managing
Director" means the Managing Director of the Corporation and includes any
person for the time being discharging the functions of the Managing Director ;
(i) "prescribed"
means prescribed by rules
(j) "regulation" means a regulation made under this Act
(k) "rule" means a
rule made under this Act ;
(l) "scheduled bank"
has the same meaning as in the State Bank of Pakistan Act, 1956 (XXXIII of
1956.) a‑
(m). "State Bank" means the State Bank of Pakistan;
established under the State Bank of Pakistan Act, 1956 (XXXIII of 1956)`; and
(n) "small business" includes
shops, workshops, cottage industries, plying of taxis and rickshaws and setting
up of professional offices.

Establishment of the corporation

PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT, 1972
PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT,
1972
3. Establishment of the Corporation.‑(1) As soon as may be
after the coming into force of this Act, the Federal Government shall establish
ire accordance with the provisions of this Act a Corporation to be called the
Peoples' Finance Corporation.
(2) The Corporation shall be a
body corporate by the name of the Peoples' Finance Corporation having perpetual
succession and a common deal, with powers, subject to the provisions of this
Act, to acquire, own and dispose of any property, and shall by the said name
sue and be sued.

Share capital

PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT, 1972
PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT,
1972
4. Share capital.‑(1) The authorised shard capital of the
Corporation shall initially be ten crores of rupees divided into ten lakh
ordinary shares of one hundred rupees
each.
(2) The paid‑up capital
of the Corporation shall, in the first instance, be five crores of rupees, out
of which three crores of rupees shall
be .contributed by the Federal Government and the remainder by the State Bank
and such of the scheduled banks as may wish to contribute.
(3) The Federal Government may,
by notification in the official Gazette, increase the authorised and paid‑up
capital of the Corporation to such extent and In such manner as may be
specified in the. notification.

Offices branches etc

PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT, 1972
PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT,
1972
5. Offices, branches, etc.‑(I) Unless the Federal'
Government, by notification in the official Gazette,, otherwise directs, the
head office of the Corporation shall be at Islamabad.
(2) The Corporation may establish regional and other offices at
such places as the Board may think fit.

Direction and superintendence

PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT, 1972
PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT,
1972
6. Direction and superintendence.‑
(1) The overall direction and superintendence of the affairs of the
Corporation shall vest in a Board of Directors constituted in accordance with
section 7, which may exercise all such powers and do all such acts and things
'as may 'be exercised and done by the Corporation arid are not by this Act
expressly directed or required to be done by the Corporation in the annual
general meeting.
(2) In discharging its
functions, the Board shall while keeping the polio` objectives of the
Corporation in view, act on business considerations.
(3) In the discharge of its functions, the Board
shall be guided on question dons of policy by the instructions, if any, given
to it by the federal Government which shall be the sole judge as to whether a
question is a question of policy.
(4) If the Board fails to carry
out the instructions given to it under sub-station (3), the Federal Government
may supersede the, Board and appoint any person or body to function in the
place of such Board until a new Board is constituted in accordance with the
provisions of this Act and no such supersession or appointment shall be
questioned in any Court.

Board

PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT, 1972
PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT,
1972
7. Board.---(1) The
Board shall consist of the following directors, namely ;‑
(a) Four persons to be
appointed by the Federal Government, of whim one shall be a; representative of
the State Bank ;
(b) Two persons to be elected,
!n such manner as .may be laid down by regulations, by the shareholders, other
than the Federal Government and the State Bank, from amongst themselves ; and
(c) the Managing Director.
(2) A Director appointed' under
clause (a) of subsection (1) shall hold office during the pleasure of the
Federal Government.
(3) A Director elected under
clause (b) of subsection (1) shall hold office for a term of three years and
shall continue in office thereafter until his successor is elected and shall be
eligible for re‑election;
Provided that such Director may
be removed before the expiration of his term by a special resolution passed by
the votes of so marry of the share holders as hold in the aggregate more than
one‑half of the shares held by the shareholders other than the, Federal
Government and the State Bank of Pakistan.
(4) A director may resign his
office by statement to that effect in writing signed by hire and addressed to
the Federal Government.
(5) A casual vacancy in the office of an elected
Director shall be filled by election and the person elected to fill such
vacancy shall hold office for the unexpired period of the term of his
predecessor.
(6) One‑of the Directors
appointed by the Federal .Government shall be nominated by the Federal
Government to be the Chairman of the Board of Directors.
(7) No act or proceeding of,
the Board shall be invalid merely on the ground of the existence of any vacancy
in, or defect in the constitution of the Board.

Managing director

PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT, 1972
PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT,
1972
8. Managing Director.‑(1) The
Managing Director shall be appointed by the Federal Government on such terms and conditions as, the Federal Government
may determine.
(2) The Managing Director
shall,
unless the Federal Government other wise directs, hold office for a
term of three years which the Federal Government may, from time to time,
extend.
(3) The Managing Director shall
be the whole‑time chief executive officer of the Corporation and shall
perform such functions as are assigned by this Act or may be assigned by the
Board :
Provided that the Federal
Government may utillse the services of the Managing Director. for any other
work.

Qualifications and disqualification of directors

PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT, 1972
PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT,
1972
9. Qualifications and disqualification of directors.‑r‑No
person shall be, or shall continue to be, a Director who‑------
(a) ' is a member of the
National Assembly or a Provincial Assembly ;
(b) is or at any time has been
adjudicated insolvent or has suspended payment or has compounded with his
creditors ;
(c) is found to be ‑,a
lunatic or becomes of unsound mind;
(d) is or has at any time been
convicted for any offence which, in the opinion of 'the Federal .Government,
is an offence involving moral turpitude ;
(e) without leave of absence
from the Board, absents himself from all the meetings of the Board for a
continuous period, of 'six months or, if less than three meetings are hold
within such period, from three, consecutive meet-lags of the Board ;
(f) has any financial or other
interest in any business to be financed by the Corporation ; or .
(g) is a salaried official of
the, Corporation, other than 'the Managing Director.

Executive committee

PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT, 1972
PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT,
1972
10. Executive
Committee. The Board shall constitute an Executive Committee consisting of
the following Directors to assist it in the discharge of its functions under
this Act, namely :----
(a) the Managing Director
(b) two directors elected by the Board out of the Directors
nominated by the Federal Government under section 7(1) (a);
(c) one director elected by,
the Board out V the directors elected under section 7(1) (b).
(2) The Managing Director
shall\ be , :the/ Chairman of the, Executive Committee.
(3) The members of the Committee‑shall hold
office for such period as may be provided by the regulations.
(4) The minutes of every meeting of the Executive
Committee shall be laid before the Board for approval at its next meeting
following the meeting of the Committee.
(5) Subject to the general and
special directions of the Board, the Execu tive Committee may deal with arty
matter within the competence of the Board.

Annual general and special meetings of shareholders

PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT, 1972
PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT,
1972
11. Annual general and special meetings of shareholders.‑(1) The
annual general meeting of the shareholders of ,the Corporation shall be held In
such date, time and place as may be
fixed by the Board, but in no case later than . six months from the date of
closing of accounts. .
(2) 'The Board shall submit‑
at the annual general meeting for the consideration of the shareholders a
statement of accounts including balance‑sheet and profit and, loss
account, and a report on the operation of
the Corpora: lion for the preceding financial year.
(3) Copies of annual statement
of accounts including balance‑sheet and profit and loss account. and
report shall be submitted soon after the holding of the annual general meeting
to the Federal Government which shall cause them to be placed before the
National Assembly. .
(4) The Board may call a
special meeting of the shareholders to be held at such time and place as it may‑fix
for consideration of any matter which, in the opinion of the Board, ought to be
considered by the shareholders, and shall call such a meeting within thirty
days of the receipt by it dl, a requisition to that affect from shareholders
holding shares not less than twenty per cent, of the paid‑up capital of
the Corporation.

Meetings of the board and executive committee

PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT, 1972
PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT,
1972
12. Meeting of the Board and Executive Committee.‑Toe meetings of
the Board and the Executive Committee shall be held as may be prescribed :
Provided that, until rules‑are
made in this behalf, such meetings shall be called, in the case of the Board.
by the Chairman and, in the case of the Executive Committee, by the Managing
Director.

Fees for attending meeting

PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT, 1972
PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT,
1972
13. Fees for attending meeting.‑The Directors 'shall be paid such
fees for attending the meetings of the Board and Executive Committee as may be
prescribed.

Secrecy and fidelity

PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT, 1972
PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT,
1972
14. Secrecy and fidelity.‑No Director shall assume
his office 'until he has made such declaration of secrecy and fidelity as may
be prescribed.

Indemnity of directors

PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT, 1972
PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT,
1972
15. Indemnity of Directors.‑A
Director shall not be personally responsible' for the acts of any other
Director or of any officer or servant of the Corporation or for any loss' or
expenditure resulting to the Corpora tion by reason of the insufficiency or
deficiency in value of or title to any property or security acquired or taken
on behalf of, the Corporation, or for anything done by him in good faith in the
discharge of his duties.

Business which the corporation can transact

PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT, 1972
PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT,
1972
16. Business which the Corporation can transact.‑Subject to
the rules, and regulations, if any, the Corporation may carry on, transact or do the 'several kinds of business and
acts hereinafter specified, namely :‑ ,
(a) To sanction loans. debts or
cash credits in-accordance with the policy either directly or through scheduled
banks under an agreement ;
(b) To guarantee a part of
loans debts and cash credits granted by the scheduled banks ,;
(c) To participate with
scheduled banks in advancing loans, debts and credits ;
(d) To purchase or otherwise
acquire, own, sell, transfer and exchange any tangible and intangible, movable or immovable property or assets. in the
discharge of its business ;
(e) To accept and furnish‑any
lien, charge, hypothecation, or mortgage of any tangible or intangible, movable
or immovable property or assets in the discharge of its business ;
(f ) To enter into agreements'
and contracts and execute such documents as may be considered necessary for the
discharge of its functions ; .
(g) To receive and pay
commissions, fees and brokerage in connection with in business ;--
(h) To invest its surplus funds in securities in the manner
prescribed ;
(i) To acquire, retain and
dispose of assets of any type which may in any way conic into the possession of
the Corporation in satisfaction or part satisfaction of any gig its claims as
lender or guarantor ;
(j) To borrow money for the purpose of its business, and to give
security for money so borrowed by pledging assets or otherwise;
(k) To acquire, maintain and
transfer its residential and business premises ;
(I) Generally to do all such
matters and things as may be incidental or subsidiary to the undertaking of any
of the aforesaid business ;
(m) to do all other acts and
things in furtherance of the purposes of this Act.

Business which the corporation cannot transact

PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT, 1972
PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT,
1972
17. Business which the Corporation cannot transact.‑The
Corporation shall not invest in shares, stocks, or debentures of companies.

Lending policy

PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT, 1972
PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT,
1972
18. Lending policy.‑(1) All classes of small business owned or
sponsored by individuals or firms having net assets not exceeding fifty
thousand rupees in value shall be eligible to receive loans from the Corporation.
Explanation.---In determining
the net assets held in the case of an individual, the assets held in the names
of his spouse and minor children shall be included and, in the case of a firm,
the assets held by all the partners in their names and in the names of their
spouses and minor children shall be included.
(2) The loan to b3 advanced to
an applicant shall in no case exceed fifty thousand rupees, and, in the case of
an applicant who has also borrowed for business, trade, profession or industry
from a financing institution or bank, the amount of the loan advanced by the
Corporation shall not exceed the difference between fifty thousand rupees and
the amount so borrowed.
(3) The period within which a
loan advanced by the Corporation shall be repayable shall not exceed eight
years.

Borrowing power

PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT, 1972
PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT,
1972
19. Borrowing power.‑(1)
The Corporation may, for the purpose of raising working capital, with the prior
approval of ‑the Federal Government, issue and sell bonds and debentures
carrying interest at such rates as may be approved by the Federal Government;
Provided that the total of the
sums due on such bonds and debentures issued and outstanding and the contingent
liabilities of the Corporation in respect of guarantees shall not, at any time,
exceed four times the aggregate of the amount of the paid‑up share
capital and the reserve fund of the Corporation.
(2) The bonds and debentures of
the Corporation shall be guaranteed
by the Federal Government as to the repayment of principal and payment of
interest at such rate as may be fixed by the Federal Government at the time the
bonds and debentures are issued.

Power to call for payment before agreed period

PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT, 1972
PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT,
1972
20. Power to call for payment before agreed period.‑Notwithstanding
any agreement to the contrary, the Corporation may, by notice, require any
borrower to whom it has granted any loan, or any person liable for payment of
such loan, forthwith to repay the loan in full, if‑
(a) It appears to the Board
that in the application for such loan false or misleading information in any
material particular has been given ; or,
(b) the borrower has failed to comply with the terms of any
agreement with the Corporation in the matter of the loan ; or
(c) for any other reason, it is
necessary, in the opinion of the Board, to protect the interest of the
Corporation.

Enforcement of claims by the corporation

PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT, 1972
PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT,
1972
21. Enforcement of claims by
the Corporation.‑Where the Corporation becomes entitled to require, the
immediate repayment of any loan before the due date and the loan is not repaid
in compliance with the‑ notice under section 20; the Corporation may
initiate proceedings in the Court of the District Judge within
the local limits of whose jurisdiction the debtor carries on :the whole or
substantial part of his business. for recovery of the whole of the outstanding
loan.

Recoveries

PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT, 1972
PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT,
1972
22. Recoveries.‑Without
prejudice to the provisions of sections 20 and 21 all sums due to the
Corporation shall be recoverable as arrears of land revenue;
Provided that no sum shall be
recovered unless fifteen days' notice has first been given by the Corporation,
td the debtor that the sum will be so recovered;
Provided further that in so
giving notice the Corporation shall inform .the debtor that he may pay such
instalments as may be fixed in the notice and that upon his so paying every
instalment on or before the. due date the recovery will by suspended but that it will otherwise proceed as
to the entire sum outstanding in case of any default in any instalment
including the .first.

Disposal of profits

PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT, 1972
PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT,
1972
23. Disposal of profits.‑(1)
The Corporation shall establish a Reserve Fund to which shall be credited such
amount out of its net annual profit, not being less than twenty‑five per
cent. of its net annual profit, as the Board may determine.
(2) The minimum appropriation
of profits to the Reserved Fund fixed under subsection (1) shall apply till
such time as the amount in the Fund equals the paid‑up capital of the
Corporation.
(3) After deducting the amount‑
under subsection (1) and making necessary provisions as are considered
expedient, the Corporation may, out of the surplus remaining from its net
annual profit, declare such dividends as may be approved by the Board.

Accounts

PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT, 1972
PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT,
1972
24. 'Accounts.‑The
Corporation shall maintain its accounts in such manner as may be prescribed.

Audit

PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT, 1972
PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT,
1972
25. Audit.‑(I) The
accounts of the Corporation shall be audited by two auditors who are chartered
accountants within the meaning of the Chartered Accountants Ordinance, 1961 (X
of 1961), appointed by the Federal Government, in consultation with the Auditor‑General,
on such remuneration, to be paid by the Corporation, as _ the Federal
Government .may fix.
(2) The Auditor‑General
shall have the power to give directions to the auditors in regard to the extent
and method of their audit subject to the provisions of the Companies Act, 1913,
and to prescribe forms of accounts to be maintained by the Corporation,
consistent with the requirements of that Act.
(3) Notwithstanding the
provisions of subsections (1) and (2), the Auditor‑General, either of his
own motion or upon a request received in this behalf from the Federal
Government may undertake such audit of the accounts of the Corporation at such
time as may be considered necessary and the Corporation shall, at the time of
such audit produce the account books,
registers and. connected documents required and furnish such
explanations and information as the Auditor‑General or an officer or
officers authorised by him in this behalf may ask four.
(4) The Corporation shall furnish
each shareholder every year with a copy of its audited account including
balance‑sheet and profit and loss account, and a report on the working of
the Corporation.

Officers and servants

PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT, 1972
PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT,
1972
26. Officers and servants.‑The
Corporation may appoint or employ such officers and servants as it considers
necessary for the efficient performance of its functions on such terms ,and
conditions as. may be laid down by regulations.

Exemption from taxes

PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT, 1972
PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT,
1972
27. Exemption from taxes.‑Notwithstanding
anything contained in the Income‑tax Act, 1922 (XI of I922), the Wealth
Tax Act, 1963 (XV of 1963), the Business Profits Tax Act, 1947 (XXI of 1947),
or any other law for the time being in force relating to income‑tax,
super tax, wealth tax, gift tax or business profits tax, the Corporation shall
not be liable to pay any such tax on its income, profits or gains.

Amendment of Act XI of 1922

PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT, 1972
PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT,
1972
28. Amendment of Act XI of
1922.‑In the Income‑tax Act, 1922 (XI of 1922), in section 15‑G,
in subsection (i), after the brackets, figures and word "(I of
1970)", the commas, words and figures ", or in the purchase of shares
issued by the Peoples' Finance Corporation established under the Peoples'
Finance Corporation Act, 1972," shall be inserted.

Shares etc to be approved securities

PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT, 1972
PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT,
1972
29. Shares, era, to be approved securities.‑Notwithstanding
anything contained in the Trusts Act, 1882 (II of 1882), the Insurance Act,
1938 (IV of 1938), and tire Banking Companies Ordinance, 1962 (LVII of 1962), the
shares and debentures of the Corporation shall be deemed to be included among
the securities enumerated in section 20 of the Trusts Act, 1882 (II of 1882),
and to be approved securities for the purposes of the Insurance Act, 1938 (IV
of 1938), , and the Banking Companies Ordinance, 1962 (LVII of 1962).

Liquidation of the corporation

PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT, 1972
PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT,
1972
30. Liquidation of the Corpora(ion.‑The Corporation shall not be
wound up save by order of the Federal Government in such manner as it may
direct.

Delegation of powers

PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT, 1972
PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT,
1972
31. Delegation of powers.‑The Board may, for the' purpose of
ensuring efficient functioning of the Corporation and facilitating 'transaction
of its daily business, by a resolution published in/ the official Gazette,
delegate to the Managing Director or any other officer of the Corporation
subject to such conditions and limitations;. if any, as may be specified
therein, such of its powers and duties under this Act as it may deem necessary.
;

Penalty and procedure

PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT, 1972
PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT,
1972
32. Penalty and Procedure.‑(I) Any person who‑----
(a) in an application for the grant of a loan gives any false or
misleading information relating to a matter which is material for the purpose
of deciding the application ; or
(b) diverts or applies the
amount of the loan granted to him to a purpose other than the purpose for which
it was granted ; or
(c) intentionally destroys, or
reduces the value of, the property on the security of which a loan was granted
to him or, without the prior approval of the Corporation in writing, or
otherwise than in accordance with the terms of such approval, transfers such
property or, any part thereof shall, without prejudice to any other action
which may be taken against him under this Act, be punishable with imprisonment
for a term which may extend to three years.
(2) No Court shall take;
cognizance of an offence punishable under subsection (1) except upon a
complaint in writing made by the Corporation pr an officer of the Corporation
authorised by it in this behalf.
sections.punishment:
punishable with imprisonment
for a term which may extend to three years.

sections.description:
Power to make rules

PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT, 1972
PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT,
1972
33. Power to make rules.‑Subject to the approval of the
Federal Government, the Board may, by notification in the official Gazette,
make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act and such rules shall be
placed before the National Assembly as soon as possible.

Power to make regulations

PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT, 1972
PEOPLES FINANCE CORPORATION ACT,
1972
34. Power to make regulations.‑(1) The Board may make
regulations to provide for all matters not required to be provided for by rules
and provision for which is necessary or expedient for carrying out the purposes of this Act.
(2) Where .any provision of the
regulations is inconsistent with any, provision of the rules, the provision of
the rules shall prevail.
